items.readable_text:
Content:
The expanded form of a decimal number expresses the number as a sum of each digit multiplied by its place value.

Content:
To illustrate, let's write the decimal number [MATH: 85.92] in expanded form. We start by writing down the place values:

Content:
| tens | ones | | tenths | hundredths |
| [MATH: 8] | [MATH: 5] | . | [MATH: 9] | [MATH: 2] |

Content:
To write the number in expanded form, we multiply each digit by its place value and add them up. So in our case, this gives:

Content:
[MATH: (8\times10) + (5\times 1) + \left(9\times \dfrac{1}{10}\right) + \left( 2\times\dfrac{1}{100}\right)]

items.readable_text:
Content:
Earlier, we expressed the decimal number [MATH: 85.92] in expanded form using fractions, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: (8\times10) + (5\times 1) + \left(9\times \dfrac{1}{10}\right) + \left( 2\times\dfrac{1}{100}\right)]

Content:
We can also represent the same number in standard form using decimals instead of fractions. To do this, we start by writing each fraction as an equivalent decimal:

Content:
[MATH: (8\times10) + (5\times 1) + \left(9\times 0.1\right) + \left( 2\times0.01\right)]

Content:
Dropping the parentheses, we get:

Content:
[MATH: 8\times10 + 5\times 1 + 9\times 0.1 + 2\times0.01]

Content:
As a final answer, this is often perfectly acceptable.

Content:
Sometimes, we might want to simplify this answer even further by evaluating each of the products. By doing this, we get

Content:
[MATH: 80 + 5 + 0.9 + 0.02.]

items.readable_text:
Content:
When zeros appear in the standard form of a decimal, they do not appear in the expanded form.

Content:
For example, [MATH: 1.{\color{blue}0}5] has a [MATH: \color{blue}0] in the tenths place.

Content:
To convert this into expanded form, we start by writing down the place values.

Content:
| ones | | tenths | hundredths |
| [MATH: 1] | . | [MATH: \color{blue}0] | [MATH: 5] |

Content:
We have:

Content:
[MATH: \qquad] [MATH: 1] one is [MATH: 1]

Content:
[MATH: \qquad] [MATH: \color{blue}0] tenths is [MATH: \color{blue}0]

Content:
[MATH: \qquad] [MATH: 5] hundredths is [MATH: 0.05]

Content:
Therefore, we get
[MATH: 1.05 = 1 + {\color{blue}0} + 0.05.]

Content:
But adding zero doesn't change a number, so we can remove it. Hence, our final answer is:
[MATH: 1.05 = 1 + 0.05.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The expanded form of a decimal number expresses the number as a sum of each digit multiplied by its place value.

Content:
To illustrate, let's write the decimal number [MATH: 85.92] in expanded form. We start by writing down the place values:

Content:
| tens | ones | | tenths | hundredths |
| [MATH: 8] | [MATH: 5] | . | [MATH: 9] | [MATH: 2] |

Content:
To write the number in expanded form, we multiply each digit by its place value and add them up. So in our case, this gives:

Content:
[MATH: (8\times10) + (5\times 1) + \left(9\times \dfrac{1}{10}\right) + \left( 2\times\dfrac{1}{100}\right)]

---

Now, to write the number in expanded form, we multiply each digit by its place value and add them up:

[MATH: (3\times 1) + \left(7\times \dfrac{1}{10}\right) + \left( 2\times\dfrac{1}{100}\right) + \left( 9\times\dfrac{1}{1,000}\right)]

Item 5 — Tutorial: Writing a Decimal Number in Standard Form as a Sum of Decimals

Content:
Earlier, we expressed the decimal number [MATH: 85.92] in expanded form using fractions, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: (8\times10) + (5\times 1) + \left(9\times \dfrac{1}{10}\right) + \left( 2\times\dfrac{1}{100}\right)]

Content:
We can also represent the same number in standard form using decimals instead of fractions. To do this, we start by writing each fraction as an equivalent decimal:

Content:
[MATH: (8\times10) + (5\times 1) + \left(9\times 0.1\right) + \left( 2\times0.01\right)]

Content:
Dropping the parentheses, we get:

Content:
[MATH: 8\times10 + 5\times 1 + 9\times 0.1 + 2\times0.01]

Content:
As a final answer, this is often perfectly acceptable.

Content:
Sometimes, we might want to simplify this answer even further by evaluating each of the products. By doing this, we get

Content:
[MATH: 80 + 5 + 0.9 + 0.02.]

EXPLANATION

| ones | | tenths | hundredths |
| [MATH: 6] | . | [MATH: 4] | [MATH: 2] |

From the table:

- [MATH: 6] ones is [MATH: 6,] which we can write as [MATH: 6\times 1]
- [MATH: 4] tenths is [MATH: 0.4,] which we can write as [MATH: 4\times 0.1]
- [MATH: 2] hundredths is [MATH: 0.02,] which we can write as [MATH: 2\times 0.01]

Therefore:
[MATH: 6.42 = 6\times 1 + 4\times 0.1 + 2\times 0.01]
